scientific_intent.scientific_task: Evaluate a generalized plasmon-pole self-energy summation at three frequencies
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: Sum complex rational pole factors times inverse-dielectric and conjugated band-amplitude products over bands, owned reciprocal vectors and plane waves; six scalar Float64 atomic reductions.
scientific_intent.discretization: Four finite small band/reciprocal-index cases, three frequencies 3/4/5, source uniform and varied signed dyadic complex coefficients, nonidentity inverse map and exact-zero control.
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: Full six output scalars against independent Decimal80 allterm oracle at predeclared 1e-11+1e-11|gold|; all input bits/guards exact, both GPU references checked on every trial.
scientific_intent.input_size_regime: (nb,ng,nc)=(3,2,31),(5,3,67),(7,4,129),(2,1,1), includes partial warp and grid-stride loops; not source512-band default or 32768-plane-wave benchmark.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float64 complex arithmetic and unordered atomic accumulation; nonsingular denominator>=7.3916, total complex condition<=7.55; no resonant/singular pole accuracy or general physical error bound.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Self-energy miniapplication extracted from BerkeleyGW electronic excited-state/material calculations. This is a kernel operator study, not a physical quasiparticle prediction or complete BerkeleyGW validation.
scientific_intent.description: Preserve unchanged native AoS and historical genuine CUDA.jl SoA operators. New independent full-frequency checker replaces original first-frequency one-sided host checker. Portable versions keep per-thread accumulators/grid-stride loops and six Float64 atomics.
scientific_intent.provenance: Repository README gpp description and MIT2019NERSC native sources. Primary background: Vergara Larrea et al., CUG2019 Experiences Porting Mini-applications..., https://cug.org/proceedings/cug2019_proceedings/includes/files/pap137s2-file1.pdf sections introduction/GPP identify BerkeleyGW General Plasmon Pole self-energy summation; no new material-science prediction claim.

algorithm: Per-thread three-complex accumulators; grid-stride bands/ownedG and 32-lane strided plane waves; six final global Float64 atomic additions.
work_item_mapping: 32 threads per (band,ownedG) block with partial plane-wave loop; case3 reduced2x2 grid exercises outer grid strides.
layout: Native CustomComplex<double> AoS x/y; all Julia models separate Float64 real/imag contiguous arrays, Int32 index maps. Each component/input/output carries 8 guards per side.
verification_contract: All20 capture 18809 Float64 words/trial: 8955 exact input/metadata prefix and 9854 full guarded outputs/inputecho. 24 outputscalars, 896physicalguards and8934 actual inputpayloadvalues/trial checked independently; exactzero control, finite denominator controls. Decimal80 allterm oracle and both GPU refs; no checksum substitute.
keyconfounds: Native AoS complex vs Julia SoA and reciprocalmultiply vs directdivision
Small finite selected kernels, not original fullCLI/physical selfenergy prediction
Float64 atomic ordering may vary between trials; tolerant numeric agreement not exact raw bitwise equality
One shared scientific helper authored during KA translation and reused by JACC; ordered workflow marginal cost
Host-inclusive sum4 short kernel dispatches; unprofiled kernel/launch/resource bottlenecks
Original native/CUDAjl first-frequency one-sided host checkers invalid as general accuracy certificates; unchanged operator independently checked
boundary_rounding_policy: inv last==nc intentionally indexes nc+1 indinv sentinel mapping to nc-1, preserved. No singular division in fixture. Exact allinputbits/guards; finite tolerant output only, no NaN pass. Atomics may reorder rounding.
support_boundary: Four named nonsingular small Float64 finite cases, three full complex frequencies. Source unusednvband remains unused; full application and singular/resonant/large configurations unverified.
interpretation: For electronic-structure users this tests the self-energy summation kernel and safe nonsingular selected data, not manybody-model accuracy. Layout and division adaptations confound abstraction comparisons; atomic-order differences are permitted only inside declared full-output error bounds. No framework limitation or measured bottleneck inferred.
